source_variants.label: unchanged-before
source_variants.hypothesis: Unchanged build A/A timing-noise control before adaptive search

source_variants.label: round-1
source_variants.hypothesis: Replace allocation-heavy per-record aggregation with borrowed-key hash aggregation: split the three fields without collecting a Vec, keep endpoint slices in the standard randomized HashMap, allocate each endpoint once when producing the result, and sort only the unique output rows. Development evidence spans 512 and 8192 records with roughly 8 to 3554 distinct endpoints; removing allocations on repeated records should improve both sizes, while expected constant-time lookup should reduce the high-cardinality tree-comparison cost. Exact numeric, Unicode-control, line-ending and invalid-row validation is unchanged.

source_variants.label: round-1-clean
source_variants.hypothesis: Replace allocation-heavy per-record aggregation with borrowed-key hash aggregation: split the three fields without collecting a Vec, keep endpoint slices in the standard randomized HashMap, allocate each endpoint once when producing the result, and sort only the unique output rows. Development evidence spans 512 and 8192 records with roughly 8 to 3554 distinct endpoints; removing allocations on repeated records should improve both sizes, while expected constant-time lookup should reduce the high-cardinality tree-comparison cost. Exact numeric, Unicode-control, line-ending and invalid-row validation is unchanged.

source_variants.label: negative-sign-shortcut
source_variants.hypothesis: Injected negative control: remove redundant-looking ASCII digit scans from the selected borrowed-key HashMap parser and trust Rust integer parsing. This can be faster but Rust accepts leading plus signs, violating the frozen strict grammar.

source_variants.label: round-2
source_variants.hypothesis: Fuse delimiter discovery, field validation, and numeric conversion into one allocation-free byte parser while retaining the incumbent borrowed-key standard HashMap and final ordering. Round-1 development measurements improve all 8192-record cases (mean case log ratios about -0.10 to -0.54), but the 512-record high-cardinality cases still regress (+0.08 to +0.17); removing repeated parser scans should lower per-record work without adding another cardinality heuristic. ASCII endpoint control checks are fused with the first-TAB scan, and non-ASCII endpoints still use char::is_control. Numeric grammar and conversion share a scan. Status values reject monotonically above 599; byte fields of at most 19 digits cannot overflow u64, and longer fields use checked arithmetic to preserve both u64::MAX and arbitrarily many leading zeroes.

source_variants.label: round-3
source_variants.hypothesis: Validate endpoint control characters only on first insertion into the per-call aggregation map. Existing keys necessarily passed the same char::is_control predicate, and exact str equality certifies subsequent occurrences without rescanning their characters. This enables the standard split_once TAB search instead of a scalar endpoint scan on every record. Round-2 development evidence leaves Unicode-endpoint cases at roughly 92-105 ns per record versus about 60-76 ns for low-cardinality ASCII cases; repeated Unicode decoding and per-record endpoint scanning are a concrete remaining cost, although this is not profiling evidence. The change can also benefit repeated ASCII endpoints while leaving numeric parsing, randomized hashing and final sorting unchanged.

source_variants.label: round-4
source_variants.hypothesis: Refine the endpoint-validation-hoisting proposal with direct recognition of the status field grammar. A valid status is exactly zero or more leading ASCII zeroes followed by [1-5][0-9][0-9] and TAB, so status arithmetic and the per-digit upper-bound loop can be replaced by direct byte checks while preserving every accepted spelling. Combined with validating each new endpoint once using char::is_control, this removes redundant parsing work on repeated and distinct endpoints. Round-3 development data reduced the Unicode-endpoint cost from round-2 roughly 92-105 ns/record to roughly 64-76, but remaining ASCII repeated-key costs around 55-65 ns/record and essentially unchanged high-cardinality costs leave plausible common-path headroom. Direct status recognition applies to all records rather than a workload-size threshold.
